verdicts.evidence: The local import binds os, and the if condition directly compares os.name at s1.
The then branch is controlled by os.name == "nt", with no negation or early exit reversing its sense.
The condition reads the operating system identifier os.name, so the os category fits.
The region is the body of the single if testing c1; there are no additional conditions in that decision. Its minimum satisfying set therefore contains one condition.
The supplied derived code places the request and execution together inside the OS check, with no alternative payload branch. The check enables those operations.
The payload runs when os.name equals nt, positively selecting the Windows target rather than checking for analysis infrastructure.
The OS condition restricts the download and execution to Windows, while ordinary installation continues after the branch. This supports targeting as the purpose of the gate.
In the supplied derived file, both the requests.get call and its enclosing exec are directly inside the then body of the same OS decision. No intervening witness hops are needed.

Both supplied files place the payload operation solely inside the OS-guarded run method; registration as the install command still enters that method through its check. There is no other call site for the derived request or execution in either file.

The supplied derived file imports requests and calls requests.get to retrieve response text. That text, after removal of pre tags, is passed directly to exec, supporting both download and execution of downloaded code.
